Reach out

Get in touch.

A question before you start, an add-on Archie doesn’t have yet, or a setup that has stopped working. The two people who build Archie read this inbox, and one of them answers you.

Support

What happens when you write in.

Support is the part of a company you only meet once something has gone wrong, which is the reason to write it down in advance rather than after. All four of these are already published: three in our operating principles, one in the Terms.

A person, within one business day

We publish a bound rather than promise to always be quick, because a promise quietly dropped is worse than a smaller one kept. Some days the answer is only that we have read it and you will have a full one by Thursday. If we are going to be slower than this for a stretch, we say so here before you find out by waiting.

You reach the people who build Archie

There is no first line that hands you to a second. Jett or Jack answers, and both of our own addresses are on this page. We keep no measure of how quickly a conversation gets closed, because that is the number that improves when you rush somebody, and asking the same question a fifth time is fine.

What support costs

Nothing. There is no paid support tier and no plan that buys you faster answers. For anything we set up with you, support at no charge and with no time limit is written into the Terms. New work is a separate thing, scoped with you first at $250 an hour, so you hear the cost before it starts and never on an invoice afterwards.

When the mistake is ours

Either of us can spend up to $500 putting one customer’s problem right, without asking the other and without accounting for it afterwards. That sits in our published principles rather than in a drawer, because an authority nobody knows about is one nobody can invoke.
